title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
mechanism: Randomise all sources of variation (data split, init, order, augmentation, hyperparameters) in every run; this cheap estimator approaches the ideal one (51x less compute) and comparisons use P(A>B).
adaptation: Each benchmark run draws a fresh grouped split and seed; methods compared by P(A>B) over paired runs instead of mean of 5 seeds on one fixed split.
min_experiment: Arm: 10 runs per method with new split+seed. Baseline: 10 seed-only runs on fixed split. Metric: share of delta variance from data split vs seed. Kill: split variance < 25% of seed variance means seed-only protocol is enough.
evidence: R: data sampling, init and hyperparameter choice all mark results; error rates of detecting improvements studied on five deep-learning tasks.
prior_overlap: none; current protocol is seed-only on a fixed split.
